questionText:
Read the following excerpt carefully and answer the question that follows:

"On 15 August 1947, as festivities erupted in New Delhi to celebrate Indian independence, Mahatma Gandhi was in Calcutta, staying in an abandoned Muslim mansion (Hydari Mansion in Beliaghata). He did not attend the midnight celebrations in Parliament, nor did he hoist the national flag. Instead, he observed a 24-hour fast and prayed for communal harmony. Riots had convulsed Bengal since the Great Calcutta Killings of August 1946. Gandhi walked barefoot from village to village in Noakhali and fasted in Calcutta, dousing the fires of communal hatred.
